assessment: Full standard-runner release feasibility not confirmed
scope: Full Windows x64 Rust release with the static-LLVM PGO repair, including fresh PGO training, distribution generation and upstream artifact tests in one standard GitHub-hosted job.

compiler_cache.type: Local sccache artifact from a preceding incomplete cold attempt

cold_attempts.outcome: Deadline during final LLVM compilation, after both PGO stages; no distribution completion
cold_attempts.cache_handoff: Failed because a redundant cache-stop operation ran after timeout cleanup; repaired before the next attempt
Succeeded; supplied the compiler cache for the restored attempts

restored_attempts.outcome: Harness CP1252 Unicode output exception interrupted artifact tests; not a timeout or demonstrated compiler failure. Fixed in the replay harness. No final release.json was written; distribution milestone is preserved in sections.json.
Deadline during upstream UI tests. release.json records exit124 and timed_out=true; no logger exception.
Deadline while WiX light.exe was building the MSI installer. No successful final-build milestone; artifact tests had not started.

conclusions: Distribution generation with the PGO repair has been observed inside360min on both Intel and AMD standard runners with this restored compiler cache.
No attempt completed all required release and artifact-test qualification. Restoring this cache is therefore not demonstrated to make the full job fit reliably.
The Intel result is promising but incomplete because of the repaired harness error; it is not a fully qualified existence proof.
Two independent AMD restored attempts missed the declared355min release budget. No further unchanged repeats were dispatched after the second AMD result.
Do not use these results to justify moving the full upstream release to the standard four-processor pool. Retain the upstream runner capacity until a separately qualified alternative exists.
limitations: A355min evidence-preserving cutoff is not the360min platform limit. These results do not prove every standard-runner allocation must fail at360min.
The cache contains entries from one incomplete cold attempt, not a fully warmed persistent upstream S3 cache. Do not generalize this cache condition to routine upstream CI.
Processor and allocation differences prevent treating these runs as paired cache-speedup or storage-speedup measurements.
PGO stage durations include compilation and profile-training work; they are not raw process-tree CPU measurements.
Historical upstream release timings used eight logical processors,32GB and a different cache condition; they do not establish a standard-runner baseline.
Post-timeout cache statistics cannot be assumed to represent the terminated build server.
No MSI installation or upgrade qualification was performed.
further_work: An explicitly Intel-conditioned standard-runner attempt could address the remaining conditional existence question, but would not establish reliability across the standard pool.
A stronger compiler-cache condition would need separately recorded seeding and provenance, while preserving fresh training and no transferred build outputs or profiles.
The x64 storage comparison remains unqualified; this assessment is not an x64 NVMe or ReFS performance result.
